text.p: General Acceptance Corp said Thursday it has requested a 15-day extension to filing its 1996 form 10-K with the Securities and Exchange Commission as it has been involved in significant negotiaitons with a potential third-party inverstor and its primary lender.
The company's discussions with the third-party investor relate to a potential investment in the form of a $10 million convertible subordinated debenture, the automobile lender said.

The company anticipates that certain principal stockholders would convert about $3 million of existing indebtedness of the company into an identical convertible subordinated debenture, the company said.

About $2 million of this $3 million was lent to the company by these stockholders during 1997. The exact terms of these transactions are still being negotiated and there can be no assurance that they will be completed, the company said.

If the investment occurs, the company said it expects its primary lender will waive the company's existing default under its revolving line of credit, and sign a new agreement granting the company a line of credit expiring January 1, 1998, the compnay said.

General Acceptance also said it expects to report a loss of about $9.1 million, or $1.51 a share, for the fiscal year ended December 31, compared with income of $717,000, or $0.13 per share, for the fiscal year ended December 31, 1995.

The loss is due to an increase in the provision for credit losses due to charge-offs in 1996 which were higher than anticipated, higher operating expenses associated with the company's efforts to strengthen its management team and further develop its infrastructure and the establishment of a valuation reserve for deferred taxes of about $4.7 million.
The company expects 1996 net revenues will be $31 million, up from $25.6 million in the previous year.
General Acceptance shares were down 13/16 at 1-11/16 on Nasdaq Thursday before being halted for pending news.
